scenarios.name: Normal Day
scenarios.subtitle: Measured demand, no injection
scenarios.description: Portfolio demand as recorded, mapped onto the network model. The reference case for the transformer risk assessment.
scenarios.teaches: Normal transformer loading and the headroom actually available.
scenarios.expected_impact: A converged load flow with every bus inside the EN 50160 band and the transformer inside nameplate. No violation, and none invented.

scenarios.name: Peak Demand
scenarios.subtitle: Coincident afternoon demand across the portfolio
scenarios.description: A broad afternoon uplift applied to the site's demand, representing the coincidence of cooling load, occupancy and process demand that produces the monthly maximum.
scenarios.teaches: That a well-sized transformer survives its own peak day. The rating was derived from the site's P99 with 25% headroom, so coincident demand alone rarely reaches nameplate -- which is precisely what sizing is for. Compare with EV Charging Surge, which is load the transformer was never sized for.
scenarios.injected_parameter: facility demand, as an additive uplift on every feeder
scenarios.magnitude: +38% of measured demand at the 15:00 centre of the bell
scenarios.expected_impact: Transformer loading rises but stays inside nameplate, because the rating was derived from the site's own P99 with headroom. The instructive result is the one where nothing breaks.

scenarios.name: EV Charging Surge
scenarios.subtitle: Fleet charging session arrives on top of site demand
scenarios.description: A block of EV charging load is added to the flexible feeder during the afternoon. It is additive: the measured site demand is untouched and both series are charted.
scenarios.teaches: The flagship case. Unlike a peak day, this is load the transformer was never sized for: it goes past nameplate, and the fix is to shift the energy rather than shed it. Deferral must also precede recovery, or the optimiser charges vehicles that have not arrived.
scenarios.injected_parameter: the flexible feeder (F4), as additive EV charging load
scenarios.magnitude: 120 kW nameplate, ramping over 30 min and tapering over 45 min
scenarios.expected_impact: The load flow puts the transformer past 100% of its calibrated capacity and pulls the LV bus down. The linear program defers EV charging into the evening -- conserving its energy as a hard equality and never recovering before it curtailed -- and buys HVAC flexibility within a comfort budget. A second, independent load flow reports the result.
